annotations.description: Hand has 5 lands and effectively only 1 castable spell (Wight of Precinct Six), since Keeper of Fables needs {3}{G}{G} with only 1 Forest. However, the hand guarantees land drops and has a turn 2 play, which in Limited is often worth keeping rather than risking a worse 6-card hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan down to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. While land-heavy, having a guaranteed turn 2 Wight and never missing land drops gives time to draw into spells. Mulliganing to 6 risks getting a worse hand with potential mana issues.

annotations.description: Bottomed a Forest from a 7-card hand that only had 2 lands, leaving just 1 land in their 6-card hand. This creates a very high risk of missing early land drops. Additionally, they have no black mana sources, making 4 of their remaining cards uncastable without drawing into Swamps.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Forest on the bottom of the library, keeping only 1 land in a 6-card hand.
annotations.betterLine: Bottom a lower-impact black card like Mind Rot or Slate Street Ruffian. Keeping both Forests ensures hitting land drops for Feral Prowler on turn 2 and gives more draw steps to find black sources.

annotations.description: Timed out and failed to play their only available land when stuck on 1 land against an opponent with 5 lands. With a hand full of 3-6 mana spells (Ravenous Chupacabra, Entomber Exarch, Mind Rot, Assassin's Strike), missing this land drop is catastrophic for catching up on mana development. The opponent already has Avalanche Caller and Marit Lage's Slumber deployed.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not play the Forest from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest immediately — it's the only legal action and there is zero downside. Every land drop is critical when this far behind on mana.

annotations.description: Cast Spark Reaper before playing a land. Playing Snow-Covered Island (or Shimmerdrift Vale) first would trigger Marit Lage's Slumber's scry 1 ability for free, providing useful information before committing to the cast. Snow-Covered Island specifically would also leave an extra untapped mana available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Spark Reaper immediately without playing a land first.
annotations.betterLine: Play Snow-Covered Island first (triggering Marit Lage's Slumber scry 1), then cast Spark Reaper with the 4 available mana.

annotations.description: Cast Suspicious Shambler (4/2) before playing a land, missing the opportunity to play a Swamp first and cast Isu the Abominable (5/5 with powerful snow synergies) this turn instead. With a Swamp played first, they'd have 5 mana (3 Islands + 2 Swamps) to cast Isu at {3}{U}{U}. Isu synergizes with Marit Lage's Slumber and Avalanche Caller, and is a vastly superior creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Suspicious Shambler (4/2 for 4 mana) without playing a land first
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Isu the Abominable ({3}{U}{U}) — a 5/5 legendary snow creature that enables playing snow cards from library top and synergizes with Marit Lage's Slumber for repeated scrying

annotations.description: Timed out on Shimmerdrift Vale's color choice, likely defaulting to White. While they can still cast Isu the Abominable with 3 Snow-Covered Islands providing the {U}{U}, choosing Blue would have provided better mana flexibility and an additional snow blue source for Avalanche Caller activations and future plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, defaulting to likely White for Shimmerdrift Vale
annotations.betterLine: Choose Blue for Shimmerdrift Vale to maximize blue mana availability for Isu the Abominable and Avalanche Caller activations, and to add another snow permanent that synergizes with Marit Lage's Slumber counting.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures (Feral Prowler is summoning sick) and only tapped lands, so both Avalanche Caller and Spark Reaper could attack with zero risk. Attacking with only Avalanche Caller deals 1 damage instead of 3, missing 2 free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Avalanche Caller (1/3) for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Avalanche Caller and Spark Reaper for 3 unblockable damage.

annotations.description: Cast Nature's Way using Feral Prowler (1 power) targeting Spark Reaper (2/3). Nature's Way deals damage equal to the creature's power, so this only deals 1 damage to a 3-toughness creature, which survives. The spell is completely wasted - it accomplishes nothing permanent.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nature's Way targeting Feral Prowler and Spark Reaper, dealing only 1 damage to a 2/3 creature that easily survives.
annotations.betterLine: Hold Nature's Way for when a bigger creature is available (e.g., Canopy Stalker at 4 power could kill any creature on opponent's board). For now, pass the turn or just play a land and develop the board toward casting black spells.

annotations.description: Only attacked with Suspicious Shambler when all three eligible creatures could safely attack. The opponent has only Feral Prowler 1/3 as a blocker and is tapped out. Avalanche Caller (1/3) and Spark Reaper (2/3) both survive blocking from a 1/3, so attacking with all three guarantees more damage with no risk of losing any creature.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Avalanche Caller, Spark Reaper, and Suspicious Shambler. Opponent can only block one, and all three survive combat with the 1/3 Feral Prowler. This pushes 3-6 additional damage through depending on blocks.

annotations.description: Missed lethal damage. Opponent is at 9 life with no creatures. GLM47 has 7 untapped lands and Avalanche Caller can be activated twice (4 mana total) to make two snow lands into 4/4 haste elementals. Attacking with both 4/4s + Spark Reaper (2 power) + Avalanche Caller (1 power) = 11 damage, which is lethal against 9 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without activating Avalanche Caller
annotations.betterLine: Activate Avalanche Caller twice targeting two Snow-Covered Islands to create two 4/4 haste elementals, then attack with all available untapped creatures (two 4/4 elementals + Spark Reaper + Avalanche Caller) for 11 damage, which is lethal.

annotations.description: GLM47 declined to activate Avalanche Caller a second time to animate another Snow-Covered Island. With the opponent at 9 life, no blockers on the field, and available attackers of two 4/4 hexproof haste elementals + Avalanche Caller 1/3 + Spark Reaper 2/3 = 11 damage, this was lethal. With only one animated land, the attack would deal at most 7 damage (not lethal).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on activating Avalanche Caller a second time, missing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Avalanche Caller targeting another Snow-Covered Island (using the 2 remaining untapped lands), then attack with both 4/4 elementals, Avalanche Caller, and Spark Reaper for 11 damage against 9 life = lethal.

annotations.description: Discarding Keeper of Fables over Mind Rot. With only 2 lands and facing lethal board threats (Isu 6/6, animated 4/4 lands), the priority is board interaction, not hand disruption. If MstMed ever reaches 5 mana, the 4/5 body of Keeper could block Isu and generate card advantage. Mind Rot doesn't affect the board at all and the opponent's threats are already deployed.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Mind Rot instead, as hand disruption is much less relevant when the opponent's threats are already on the battlefield and you need board presence to survive.

annotations.description: The opponent is at 9 life with no creatures on the battlefield and only 2 untapped Forests. GLM47 has Isu the Abominable (6/6) and Avalanche Caller which can turn a snow land into a 4/4 hexproof haste creature for {2}. That's 10 damage against 9 life with no blockers — lethal on board. annotations.actionTaken: Played a Swamp (and apparently activated Spark Reaper) during precombat main instead of attacking for lethal.
